title: Snake-normalized support boundary and unit-induced section comparison
statement:
Use the kernel-of-restriction construction of supported sections [def-pur-support-cohomology] and the cochain derived-category convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a site $(\mathcal C,J)$, a commutative coefficient ring $A$, and an arrow $j:W	o V$, a family $\delta^q:H^q(W,-)	o H^{q+1}_{V\setminus W}(V,-)$ of natural $A$-linear boundary maps on bounded-below complexes is snake-normalized if, for every bounded-below complex $I$ of injective $A$-module sheaves, the termwise sequence
$$0	o\ker(I(V)	o I(W))	o I(V)	o I(W)	o0$$
is short exact and its cochain snake connecting map in every integer degree $q$ equals $\delta^q$ transported to this injective model by the canonical right-derived comparison maps. This defines a predicate on a given boundary family, not an existence assertion about it.

For any scheme $T$ and its etale/pro-etale comparison adjunction $
u_T^*\dashv
u_{T,*}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], any ring $A$ and any etale $T$-object $V$, define the section comparison $F(V)	o(
u_T^*F)(V)$ by evaluating the adjunction unit $F	o
u_{T,*}
u_T^*F$ at $V$. Define its bounded-below derived comparison by right-derived base change, and its degree-$q$ section-hypercohomology comparison by applying $H^q$, for every $q\in\mathbf Z$. These are specified maps, with no finite-type hypothesis on $T$ and no finiteness hypothesis on $A$.
